author.bio: Omar leads the compliance desk at Basmat Al Mawared, guiding employers through Qiwa, Muqeem and Nitaqat processes with more than 12 years of experience in Saudi labor law and workforce management.

body.h2: How a manpower partner simplifies the process
body.p1: Transferring employees between sponsors in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia is a routine yet highly regulated process. With the Qiwa platform now serving as the single digital gateway for labor services, employers must keep their records current to avoid penalties and service interruptions.
body.p2: A Muqeem transfer is the practical step that follows approval on Qiwa: the employee's sponsor record is updated with the Ministry of Interior, the worker receives the updated residence permit (Iqama), and the new sponsor assumes full responsibility for the worker.
body.p3: Basmat Al Mawared's compliance desk manages every transfer end to end, achieving clearances in as little as a few business days. Because we maintain continuous records on Qiwa and Muqeem, transferred workers are deployable immediately upon completion, with zero gaps in legal status.
body.p4: Inaccurate or delayed transfer records trigger Ministry of Labor warnings, affect your Nitaqat classification, and can halt the mobility of your entire workforce. Keeping a single accountable partner who processes every transfer correctly protects both your compliance rating and your project timelines.
body.p5: From GOSI and medical bookings to insurance, WPS payroll and end-of-service benefits, a dedicated manpower supplier bundles every administrative step. Employers focus on operations while the partner guarantees 100% MLSD-compliant, background-checked personnel at every site.
body.quote: The fastest, most compliant way to onboard transferred staff is to hand the full process - Qiwa approvals, Muqeem records, medical, insurance and Iqama updates - to a licensed manpower partner.

cookiePolicy.noAnalytics: No analytics are installed on this website at present. There is no Google Analytics, no Meta Pixel, no advertising tag and no heatmap tool. s1.text: A cookie is a small text file a website stores on your device. Related technologies such as local storage work the same way in practice: they keep a small amount of information in your browser between visits. Throughout this policy we use the word “cookies” to cover both, because what matters to you is what is stored and why, not the technical mechanism.

s3.functionalText: These improve the experience but are not essential. Today this covers only the CV Builder draft saved on your own device. If you decline, the website still works fully — your CV draft simply is not kept between visits. Our company video is self-hosted and needs no consent.
s3.necessaryText: These make the website work and cannot be switched off. They remember your cookie choice and help protect our forms from automated abuse. They store nothing that identifies you personally and are never used for marketing.

s4.noAds: We do not use advertising networks, social media tracking pixels, data brokers, or any service that profiles you across other websites.

cvBuilder.whyP1: Applicant Tracking Systems read a CV as plain text before any human sees it. Anything that breaks that reading — a photo, a two-column layout, a logo, text inside a table or a CV saved as an image — can cause an otherwise strong candidate to be filtered out automatically.
cvBuilder.whyP2: Every template here is single-column, uses standard section headings the software expects, and exports as selectable text rather than a picture of text. That is the difference between being read and being discarded.
